title: Egypt in Full — Cairo, the Nile, the Eclipse & the Red Sea
intro: Fourteen days, built around one Monday. Five nights in Cairo and Giza open it — the plateau and the Grand Egyptian Museum, Memphis and Sakkara, a day on the Mediterranean at Alexandria, and the Royal Mummies at Fustat. Then south to Aswan for Abu Simbel and a three-night cruise down through Kom Ombo and Edfu to Luxor. On 2 August you are at Karnak for the total eclipse — among the columns of the Great Hypostyle Hall, close to the point of greatest duration on this eclipse and one of the longest of the century. That afternoon you cross to the Red Sea for five all-inclusive nights in Hurghada with nothing at all on the schedule. Private guide and vehicle throughout, never a group.

arrival.title: Arrival in Cairo — Sunday 25 July
arrival.description:
Arrival at Cairo International Airport.
Meet & assist by our representative airside, who stays with you through the visa, passport and customs formalities and collects your luggage with you.
Private air-conditioned transfer to your hotel.
Nothing scheduled — time to settle in and sleep off the flight before an early start tomorrow.
Welcome dinner at the hotel.
Overnight in Cairo.
arrival.hotel: Pyramids Park Resort Cairo, 4★ (or equal) — bed & breakfast

days.title: The Giza Plateau & the Grand Egyptian Museum — Monday 26 July
days.description:
Breakfast at the hotel, then meet your private licensed Egyptologist.
The Giza Plateau: the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure, and the panoramic viewpoint where all three line up at once. Entry into a burial chamber is available on the spot, at extra cost.
The Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple of Khafre, where the causeway ends in limestone blocks the size of a small car.
Lunch at a local restaurant overlooking the plateau.
The Grand Egyptian Museum: the hanging obelisk, the Ramses II atrium, the grand staircase of royal statuary, and the complete Tutankhamun collection shown together for the first time — over five thousand objects with the death mask among them.
Back to the hotel; evening at leisure. Overnight in Cairo.
days.hotel: Pyramids Park Resort Cairo, 4★ (or equal) — bed & breakfast

days.title: Memphis, Sakkara & Dahshur — Tuesday 27 July
days.description:
Breakfast, then south along the west bank with your Egyptologist.
Memphis, capital of the Old Kingdom: the colossal recumbent Ramses II in his own pavilion and the alabaster sphinx, in a village of palm groves where the city once ran for miles.
Sakkara: the Step Pyramid of Djoser — the first monumental stone building anywhere — the Serapeum, and the mastaba tombs whose painted reliefs of harvest, cattle and market days are still sharp after four and a half thousand years.
Lunch at a local restaurant.
Dahshur, where the geometry was worked out: the Bent Pyramid, whose builders changed the angle halfway up, and the Red Pyramid, the first true smooth-sided pyramid, which you may enter at no extra charge.
Back to the hotel. Overnight in Cairo.
days.hotel: Pyramids Park Resort Cairo, 4★ (or equal) — bed & breakfast

days.title: Alexandria — a Day on the Mediterranean — Wednesday 28 July
days.description:
Early breakfast, then the desert road north — around three hours to the coast.
The Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa: a shaft cut a hundred feet down into three storeys of Roman-era tombs, with the spiral stair around the well, the banqueting triclinium, and a burial chamber where Egyptian gods stand in Roman dress.
Pompey's Pillar and the Serapeum, with the underground galleries of the daughter library.
The Bibliotheca Alexandrina, the modern answer to the ancient library: the great tilted disc of the reading room on eleven cascading terraces, and the granite wall carved with the scripts of the world.
Seafood lunch on the Corniche, at a fish market where you pick from the ice and they cook it.
The Citadel of Qaitbay on the foundations of the Pharos lighthouse, then back along the Corniche past the Stanley Bridge and the gardens of Montazah.
Overnight in Cairo.
days.hotel: Pyramids Park Resort Cairo, 4★ (or equal) — bed & breakfast

days.title: Egyptian Civilization, Coptic & Islamic Cairo — Thursday 29 July
days.description:
Breakfast, then the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization at Fustat: one gallery running the whole length of Egypt, and below it the Royal Mummies Hall — twenty kings and queens in low light and climate control, Ramses II and Hatshepsut among them.
Lunch at a local restaurant.
Coptic Old Cairo on foot: the Hanging Church suspended on the towers of the Roman fortress, the Church of St Sergius over the crypt where the Holy Family is held to have sheltered, and the Ben Ezra Synagogue — three faiths inside two hundred metres.
Al-Moez Ldin Allah Street, the open-air museum of medieval Cairo: Bayt Al-Suhaymi, the Qalawun complex and the minarets of Al-Hakim, ending in Khan El-Khalili for mint tea at El-Fishawy among the coppersmiths and the spice sellers.
Early night — tomorrow starts before dawn. Overnight in Cairo.
days.hotel: Pyramids Park Resort Cairo, 4★ (or equal) — bed & breakfast

days.title: To Aswan — the High Dam & Philae — Friday 30 July
days.description:
Breakfast box and check-out for the morning flight south, met at Aswan and driven straight to the mooring.
Check-in by noon, with a welcome from the front office team and a quick orientation of the boat so you know where everything is.
Lunch in the main restaurant to charge your energy after the flight.
The afternoon out: the Aswan High Dam and the granite quarries, then the Temple of Philae, reached by motorboat to Agilkia Island — cut into blocks and rebuilt stone by stone to save it from the rising water, the last temple in Egypt where the old religion was practised.
Back aboard for an à la carte dinner, followed by a live band, oriental music and a tanoura performance in the lounge bar.
Overnight in Aswan.
days.hotel: Sonesta Nile cruise, 5★ (or equal) — full board

days.title: Abu Simbel, then Sailing to Kom Ombo — Saturday 31 July
days.description:
Abu Simbel this morning, and included rather than optional. An early start south across the desert, roughly three hours each way, to the two temples cut whole into the cliff for Ramses II and Nefertari — four twenty-metre seated colossi at the facade, the Battle of Kadesh across the inner walls, and a sanctuary the entire mountain was sliced into blocks and lifted clear of the rising lake.
The open buffet breakfast is there for whoever would rather sleep, and there is plenty of it.
Back aboard around midday and the ship casts off for Kom Ombo — ice cream on the sundeck as you sail, then the traditional lunch, oriental cooking done properly.
Once docked, your visit to the Temple of Kom Ombo: the only double temple in Egypt, halved precisely between the two gods Sobek the crocodile and Haroeris the elder Horus, with the surgical instruments carved on the outer wall.
Back for an à la carte dinner, then the galabya party, live music and cocktails in the lounge bar.
Overnight in Edfu.
days.hotel: Sonesta Nile cruise, 5★ (or equal) — full board

days.title: Edfu, a Cooking Class & Luxor Temple — Sunday 1 August
days.description:
A light breakfast, then the Temple of Horus at Edfu by horse carriage from the mooring — the most completely preserved temple in Egypt, with its pylon, courtyard, black granite falcon and the roofed sanctuary still holding the barque shrine.
Back aboard to find the executive chef waiting: a cooking class, and an Egyptian dish or two you can actually reproduce at home.
Ice cream on the sundeck afterwards, then the barbecue — a spread of properly grilled things eaten in the open air as the ship works north.
The east bank in the evening: Luxor Temple, with the standing obelisk of Ramses II at the gate and the Roman and Islamic city built straight over the top of it. Lit after dark it is the best hour to see it.
Then the gala dinner, followed by a folklore show, a tanoura performance and live music in the lounge.
An early night: tomorrow is the reason for the dates. Overnight in Luxor.
days.hotel: Sonesta Nile cruise, 5★ (or equal) — full board

days.title: Totality at Karnak — the West Bank, then the Red Sea — Monday 2 August
days.description:
Breakfast with the Nile going by, then check-out; your luggage travels with the vehicle for the rest of the day.
Your Egyptologist takes you across to the west bank early, while it is cool and empty: the Valley of the Kings, its royal tombs cut deep into the hillside with painted corridors and star-vaulted ceilings intact, and the Temple of Queen Hatshepsut at El-Deir El-Bahari.
The Colossi of Memnon on the way back, the two seated quartzite giants of Amenhotep III out on the flood plain.
Then across to Karnak in good time, well before the approaches close — the avenue of ram-headed sphinxes, the first pylon, and the Great Hypostyle Hall.
And there you stay for the eclipse: shade rigged and cold water for all three of you.
The partial phases run for over an hour, the light goes wrong, the birds stop — then totality, over the temple of Amun-Ra. Luxor lies close to the point of greatest duration on this eclipse.
We let the roads clear rather than fight them, then a late lunch and the transfer east to Hurghada, roughly four hours across the desert.
Check-in on an all-inclusive basis, for five nights with nothing on the schedule. Overnight in Hurghada.

days.title: Hurghada — Orange Island & the Dolphin Banks — Tuesday 3 August
days.description:
Breakfast at the resort, and from here the pace is entirely yours: everything below is offered, nothing is compulsory.
Optional today, at extra cost: a full-day boat out to Orange Island, the sandbank lagoon off Hurghada with its long wooden jetty and shallow turquoise water.
Two swim stops over the reefs with equipment provided and a guide in the water, and dolphin watching at the offshore banks where spinner pods gather through the morning — wild sightings, so never guaranteed.
Lunch served on board, back to the resort mid-afternoon.
Otherwise: the private beach, the pools, the house reef and the spa, all included.
Dinner at the resort. Overnight in Hurghada.

days.title: Hurghada — the Eastern Desert, or Nothing at All — Wednesday 4 August
days.description:
Breakfast at the resort.
Optional, at extra cost: an afternoon in the Eastern Desert — quad bikes or a 4x4 out across the flats toward the Red Sea mountains, a Bedouin settlement, a camel ride if you want one, and dinner under the stars with the desert sky doing what it does out there.
Optional instead: a submarine or glass-bottom boat trip over the coral gardens, with no swimming needed.
Or nothing. The resort is all-inclusive and the day costs you nothing extra if you spend it on a sunbed.
Overnight in Hurghada.

days.title: Hurghada — Giftun Island & the Reefs — Thursday 5 August
days.description:
Breakfast at the resort.
Optional today, at extra cost: Giftun Island and the national park reefs, the best snorkelling within reach of Hurghada — two or three stops, equipment and a guide in the water, lunch on board.
For anyone who would rather go under properly, the dive centre can arrange an introductory dive with an instructor, or a certified boat dive.
Back in the afternoon; the rest of the day at the resort.
Dinner at the resort. Overnight in Hurghada.

days.title: Hurghada at Leisure — Friday 6 August
days.description:
Your last full day, and deliberately empty.
Breakfast whenever you surface, then the beach, the pools, the spa, or the Marina promenade and the old town in the evening if you want to be somewhere else for a couple of hours.
Everything at the resort is included; anything off-site your host can arrange at short notice.
A good day to pack slowly and eat well.
Dinner at the resort. Overnight in Hurghada.

departure.title: Departure — Saturday 7 August
departure.description:
Breakfast at the resort, subject to your flight timing; a breakfast box is arranged for an early departure.
Check-out, with a late check-out requested where the resort can give it.
Private air-conditioned transfer to Hurghada International Airport for your flight home, or to Cairo for an onward international connection — whichever your ticketing needs, with meet & assist at both ends.
Final assistance through check-in and departure formalities. Safe journey home.
